targetAudience.primary: Runtime, orchestration and platform engineers operating selectable execution environments
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands process environments, configuration precedence and durable task resume.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A turn can execute in one resolved environment while inheriting process-variable policy from another scope, creating split-brain configuration authority.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change moves ShellEnvironmentPolicy into EnvironmentConfig and routes regular shell, user-shell and unified-exec construction through the selected environment with an explicit fallback.

externalHook.description: Selecting an execution environment is incomplete if subprocess configuration still comes from a stale thread-global owner.

coreProposition: Execution-scoped configuration should follow the resolved environment that owns the work, with explicit fallback and precedence plus a stable policy identity for durable resume.

originalValue.description: Frames execution context as a configuration-authority boundary and separates selected-environment ownership, fallback, precedence, provenance and confidentiality controls.

readerTakeaway: Bind every subprocess launcher to a declared environment policy source, make fallback and merge order visible, compare policy identity during resume and treat debug redaction as only one observability safeguard.

supported: EnvironmentConfig carries ShellEnvironmentPolicy and redacts it from Debug output.
Three shell execution paths consume the selected turn environment policy with a session-derived fallback.
Tests use conflicting policies to show that selected-environment filtering wins while its explicit values survive.
unsupported: Secret non-disclosure across output and telemetry
uncertain: Coverage of MCP servers, hooks and other integrations
The correct policy-fingerprint and resume response contract

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument applies generally to runtimes with selectable execution environments and does not require a first-party project.

decisionReason: The implementation provides concrete ownership and precedence evidence, while the Research Object adds a bounded configuration-authority model useful beyond the source patch.
